_meta.description: Material models for an O-band SOI microring modulator, 273-400 K. Cleaned copy of docs/research/02_materials.json with the verification-log corrections of 02_materials.md and the decisions of 07_design_critique.md (P1-6, P1-7, P1-9, P1-11, D20) applied. mrm/materials.py reads every coefficient from this file.

conventions.wavelength: coefficients use lam in um (as printed); the mrm.materials API takes lam_m (vacuum wavelength, m)
conventions.index_level: recommended silicon index is on the Frey 2006 / Franta 2017 absolute (vacuum) level; fused silica is Malitson x n_air (absolute), so both are vacuum-referenced
conventions.reference_values: values printed or derived in 02_materials.md; tests/verification/test_materials.py reproduces them
conventions.provenance_words: printed / read-off / inferred / derived / assumed (02_materials.md header)

corrections_applied: 02 log #14: thin-film Si conductivity re-anchored to Aubain & Bandaru 2010 (260 nm: 90 +/- 10 W/mK); d0 = 170 nm (was 250 nm); 84 W/mK at 220 nm, 300 K; +/-15 % (was 69 W/mK, +/-25 %).

07 P1-3 prints 'thin-film k 56-66 W/mK for 150-200 nm (+/-25 %)'; that text predates the 02 correction and is superseded: the corrected fit gives 71.8 (160 nm) and 80.0 (200 nm) W/mK at 300 K, +/-15 %.

02 log #6: material group index n_g,Si uncertainty widened to +/-0.02; Li gives 3.674, Frey/Franta 3.689/3.690. The recommended index model (Li shape on Frey level) gives 3.690 and is the one used everywhere (07 P1-6).
02 log #2: Li 1980 dL/L293 constant read as -0.071 % = -7.1e-4.
02 log #5: Li appears air-referenced, Frey is absolute (vacuum); about 0.9e-3 of the 4.1e-3 offset is the air/vacuum convention. The recommended model is vacuum-referenced.
02 log #3: Franta 2017 rises only +12 % over 273-400 K (Li +17 %); the dn/dT slope beta is uncertain (1.0e-3 to 1.45e-3 /K), recorded in si_dn_dt_slope.
02 log #7: thermal-shift ceiling: strict all-silicon limit (neff/ng = n_Si/n_g,Si) added: 72.3/79.2/81.1 pm/K.
02 §2.2 checker note: the ceiling must take n_g,Si from the same index model as n; mrm.materials.dlambda_dt_ceiling_pm_per_k defaults to the recommended model (Li-only values kept as references).
02 log #16: Corning prints both 1.30 and 1.38 W/mK for 7980; 1.38 (Palankovski) is nominal, 1.30 an alternative.
02 log #23 and 07 D20: Ge dark-current Ea nominal 0.37 eV, range 0.35-0.38 eV; Balbi 2009 (x1.9 per 10 C, Ea up to ~0.5 eV) kept as a stress value; I_d0 = 1-30 nA at 25 C (GF prints < 30 nA).
02 log #20: Borghi 2021 tau_th = 270 ns is a one-pole fit with an inflated sigma_FCD, not a measured pole.
06 §2.6 (corrected): Souza 2018 Si CTE 2.5e-6 /K at 300 K, net +27 %/100 K, added as an alpha_L cross-check.
07 P1-11: heater TCR tied to the heater family (doped Si 1.0-1.8e-3, TiN ~0.5e-3, silicides and W 2-4.5e-3 /K).
SiO2 alpha_L(T): linear model inferred from the two printed Corning means (0.52 ppm/K over 5-35 C, 0.57 ppm/K over 0-200 C); 02 gave only the means.

Li 1980 20-293 K dL/L branch is not used: the 293-1600 K branch reproduces Li Table 1 at 250 K to 1e-4 and differs from the (percent-corrected) low branch by < 4e-6 in n at 250-293 K; one smooth branch keeps dn/dT continuous.

si_index_li1980.quantity: refractive index of crystalline Si, Li 1980 formula (temperature shape)
si_index_li1980.model: n^2 = eps(T) + (L(T)/lam^2)*(A0 + A1*T + A2*T^2); eps = e0 + e1*T + e2*T^2 + e3*T^3; L = exp(-3*dLL); dLL = c0 + c1*T + c2*T^2 + c3*T^3 (lam in um, T in K)

printed_checks.note: Li 1980 Table 1 (printed) at 1.20 um and 1.30 um; Table 2 dn/dT at 1.30 um, 400 K

si_index_li1980.valid_range_note: 1.2-14 um; 100-750 K recommended (L branches cover 20-1600 K); this implementation uses the 293-1600 K dL/L branch throughout (validated against Table 1 down to 250 K)
si_index_li1980.source: H. H. Li, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 9, 561 (1980), eq. (22), Table 1
si_index_li1980.notes: printed as -0.071; must be read as -0.071 % (-7.1e-4) to reproduce Li's Table 1 (derived check). Li appears air-referenced (02 log #5).

si_index_frey2006.quantity: refractive index of crystalline Si, Frey 2006 temperature-dependent Sellmeier (absolute level)
si_index_frey2006.model: n^2 - 1 = sum_{i=1..3} S_i(T) lam^2/(lam^2 - lam_i(T)^2); S_i, lam_i = 4th-order polynomials in T
si_index_frey2006.valid_range_note: 1.1-5.6 um, 20-300 K ONLY (polynomials diverge near 325 K)
si_index_frey2006.uncertainty_note: absolute +/-1e-4 (Table 1: 8.67e-5 at 1.5 um, 295 K); fit residual 1e-4
si_index_frey2006.source: B. J. Frey, D. B. Leviton, T. J. Madison, Proc. SPIE 6273, 62732J (2006), Tables 2, 4, 5 (arXiv:physics/0606168)
si_index_frey2006.notes: Sellmeier dn/dT at 293 K (1.82e-4) undershoots the paper's own measured Table 4 (1.94e-4 at 1.3 um, 295 K). Used only at 295 K, to set the absolute level of the recommended model.

si_index_recommended.quantity: recommended Si index: Li 1980 temperature shape on the Frey 2006 / Franta 2017 absolute level
si_index_recommended.model: n_Li(lam,T) + [n_Frey(lam,295K) - n_Li(lam,295K)] (07 P1-6: one silicon index model everywhere; n, n_g and dn/dT all from it)

crosschecks.note: Franta 2017 (refractiveindex.info, built on Frey's data) sides with the Frey level; Green 2008 with Li's. Our recommended level is Frey's.

si_index_recommended.valid_range_note: 1.26-1.36 um, 273-400 K (design envelope); the Frey offset itself is defined over 1.1-5.6 um
si_index_recommended.uncertainty_note: +/-5e-4 absolute (derived); Li vs Frey disagree by 4.1e-3 at 1310 nm, 2x Li's stated uncertainty. The Li level is the alternative hypothesis (level='li'); never mix the two inside one ring calculation. A 4e-3 index change moves a design resonance by 1.2-1.4 nm.
si_index_recommended.source: Li 1980 + Frey 2006; Franta et al., Appl. Surf. Sci. 421, 405 (2017) agrees with Frey level (3.50555 at 300 K)

si_dn_dt.quantity: thermo-optic coefficient of Si at 1310 nm
si_dn_dt.model: analytic temperature derivative of Li 1980 eq. (22); the Frey offset is temperature-independent, so the recommended model has the same dn/dT

crosschecks.note: low corner Franta, high corner Lukes; Wang 2025 thin-film value is a single noisy sample (flag, not a datum)

si_dn_dt.uncertainty_note: recommended 1.94e-4 +/-0.07e-4 at 300 K; 2.13e-4 +/-0.1e-4 at 375 K (spread of sources)
si_dn_dt.source: Li 1980; cross-checks: Frey 2006 Table 4 = 1.94e-4 (1.3 um, 295 K, printed); Franta 2017 = 1.87e-4 (300 K) / 2.00e-4 (375 K) (read-off+derived); Lukes 1959/60 = 2.04e-4 (1.327 um, 300 K, printed in Li Table A-3); Cocorullo 1999 at 1523 nm = 1.855e-4 (300 K), scaled to 1310 nm = 1.95e-4 (derived); Wang 2025 SOI 224 nm film ~2.3e-4 (298-338 K, derived, noisy)
si_dn_dt.notes: Textbook REF.dnSi_dT = 1.86e-4 is the 1523 nm, 300 K value (Cocorullo 1999). Della Corte group (1.5 um) found no dependence on doping type/level/orientation.

si_d2n_dt2.quantity: second temperature derivative of the Si index at 1310 nm
si_d2n_dt2.uncertainty_note: sources span 1.7e-7 to 2.8e-7 (Franta 1.88e-7 at 300 K, 1.70e-7 at 375 K; Cocorullo 1523 nm 2.58e-7 at 300 K, 2.35e-7 at 375 K)
si_d2n_dt2.source: Li 1980; Franta 2017; Cocorullo, Della Corte, Rendina, APL 74, 3338 (1999)

si_dn_dt_slope.quantity: normalized slope of silicon dn/dT, beta = (d2n/dT2)/(dn/dT), the gain-schedule shape of 07 R1
si_dn_dt_slope.model: beta(T) = d2n_dT2 / dn_dT from the recommended (Li-shape) model

crosschecks.note: Souza et al., Nat. Commun. 9, 665 (2018) supplementary: dn/dT = 1.8e-4 + 2.4e-7 dT - 2.1e-10 dT^2 (06 §2.6, printed); Franta from the 02 refit (d2n/dT2 1.87e-7 over dn/dT 1.871e-4). 07 R1 uses beta ~1.4e-3 /K.

si_dn_dt_cocorullo1523.quantity: thermo-optic coefficient of Si at 1523 nm (cross-check only)
si_dn_dt_cocorullo1523.source: G. Cocorullo, F. G. Della Corte, I. Rendina, Appl. Phys. Lett. 74, 3338 (1999)

si_group_index.quantity: material group index of Si, n_g = n - lam dn/dlam
si_group_index.model: analytic wavelength derivative of the chosen index model
si_group_index.uncertainty_note: +/-0.02 [corrected by checker from +/-0.01: Frey 2006 Sellmeier gives 3.689 at 1.31 um, 295 K; Franta 2017 gives 3.690 at 300 K; both ~0.016 above Li]
corrections: 02 log #6: +/-0.01 widened to +/-0.02; recommended model gives 3.690 at 300 K (Frey/Franta level)

si_absorption_band.quantity: band-to-band absorption of Si (not the ring loss)
si_absorption_band.uncertainty_note: order of magnitude; 300 K; band edge moves ~27 meV red by 400 K, still < ~0.02 dB/cm at 1260 nm (derived estimate)
si_absorption_band.source: M. A. Green, Sol. Energy Mater. Sol. Cells 92, 1305 (2008)

ring_thermal_shift_ceiling.quantity: upper bound of dlambda/dT for any Si-core, SiO2-clad ring at 1310 nm
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling.model: dlam/dT <= lam*(dn_Si/dT)/n_g,Si + lam*(neff/ng)*alpha_Si  (all electric energy in Si; first-order perturbation with material dispersion)
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling.uncertainty_note: -2 to -4 pm/K with Franta dn/dT; +3 pm/K with Lukes at 300 K; with the Frey/Franta group index (3.690) the thermo-optic part drops by about 0.3 pm/K
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling.source: this file, from Li 1980 and Okada & Tokumaru 1984
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling.notes: In GHz/K: 12.4 (300 K), 13.6 (375 K), 13.9 (400 K). Lightmatter M4B.3 prints '~15 GHz/C' (85.8 pm/K) in its introduction; that is 1.08-1.26x above this ceiling over 273-400 K and needs dn_Si/dT ~2.35e-4, which Li reaches only near 500 K.
corrections: 02 log #7: strict all-Si limit (neff/ng = n_Si/n_g,Si = 0.953) gives 72.3/79.2/81.1 pm/K

crosschecks.note: Malitson x n_air (1.00027) reproduces the absolute CHARMS index to 1e-5 at 295 K

sio2_index_malitson.uncertainty_note: +/-1e-5 vs CHARMS after air correction (derived check)
sio2_index_malitson.source: I. H. Malitson, JOSA 55, 1205 (1965); Leviton & Frey arXiv:0805.0091 (1.44845 at 1.2 um, 1.44502 at 1.5 um, 295 K)

sio2_index_films.model: fused-silica dispersion shifted to the film level at 1310 nm, 295 K
sio2_index_films.uncertainty_note: +/-0.01 between processes; thermal oxide within a few 1e-3 of fused silica
sio2_index_films.source: Rodriguez-de Marcos et al., Opt. Mater. Express 6, 3622 (2016); Franta et al., Proc. SPIE 9890, 989014 (2016); Arbabi & Goddard, Opt. Lett. 38, 3878 (2013)

sio2_dn_dt.model: dn/dT = base + slope*(T - 295); thermal/fused base 8.45e-6, PECVD/BEOL base 0.95e-5
sio2_dn_dt.valid_range_note: measured 30-310 K (fused silica, 1.2-1.5 um); linear extension above 300 K is assumed
sio2_dn_dt.uncertainty_note: RT values span 0.84e-5 (Leviton) to 0.96e-5 (Corning, PECVD); +/-15 %. A +/-15 % error moves the ring sensitivity by < ~1 pm/K.
sio2_dn_dt.source: Leviton & Frey arXiv:0805.0091 Table 6 (8.40-8.45e-6 at 295 K); Corning 7980 data sheet 9.6e-6 at 1128.64 nm (polynomial gives 9.53e-6 at 1310 nm, inferred); Arbabi & Goddard 2013 PECVD (0.95+/-0.10)e-5; Elshaari 2016 PECVD (0.96+/-0.09)e-5

si3n4_index_luke.quantity: LPCVD Si3N4 index (only if nitride sits in the mode)
si3n4_index_luke.source: K. Luke et al., Opt. Lett. 40, 4823 (2015)

si3n4_dn_dt.source: Arbabi & Goddard, Opt. Lett. 38, 3878 (2013); Elshaari et al., IEEE Photonics J. (2016)

si_alpha_l.quantity: linear thermal expansion coefficient of Si (the substrate clamps the ring length to it)

crosschecks.note: Souza et al. 2018 supplementary (06 §2.6, corrected): 2.5e-6 /K at 300 K, net +27 % per 100 K

si_alpha_l.source: Y. Okada, Y. Tokumaru, J. Appl. Phys. 56, 314 (1984)

sio2_alpha_l.quantity: linear thermal expansion coefficient of SiO2 (fused silica; thermal oxide assumed similar)
sio2_alpha_l.model: alpha(T) = a293 + slope*(T - 293.15); a293 = mean over 5-35 C, slope from the 0-200 C mean (inferred from the two printed means)
sio2_alpha_l.uncertainty_note: +/-0.05e-6 (printed means); PECVD oxide is process dependent

thermo_mechanical.quantity: expansion and photoelastic contributions to the ring shift
thermo_mechanical.model: expansion: lam*(neff/ng)*alpha_Si; photoelastic: oxide biaxial stress E/(1-nu)*(alpha_Si-alpha_SiO2) ~0.18 MPa/K times stress-optic 1e-12..4e-12 /Pa
thermo_mechanical.valid_range_note: SOI ring on thick Si substrate
thermo_mechanical.uncertainty_note: photoelastic part is an order-of-magnitude estimate (<~1 pm/K), no source
thermo_mechanical.source: derived; E, nu and stress coefficient (35.0 nm/(cm MPa)) printed on Corning 7980 data sheet

k_si_bulk.uncertainty_note: +/-5 % (handbook values vary 68.8-157 per Electronics Cooling 1998; Glassbrenner & Slack 1964 ~156 at 300 K is recalled, not re-checked)
k_si_bulk.source: V. Palankovski, PhD thesis TU Wien (2000) sec. 3.2.3; consistent with CRC/TPRC set 168/148/98.9 at 273/300/400 K (quoted from memory, assumed)

k_si_film.quantity: in-plane thermal conductivity of a single-crystal SOI film (device layer)

crosschecks.note: the fit gives 45 W/mK at 74 nm and 105 W/mK at 420 nm: use it only for 150-300 nm

k_si_film.valid_range_note: single-crystal SOI film 150-300 nm, 273-400 K, undoped to ~1e18 cm^-3
k_si_film.uncertainty_note: +/-15 % (73-95 W/(m K) at 220 nm, 300 K, from the +/-10 W/(m K) of the anchor measurement). 300 to 375 K: -13 % at 220 nm, -12 % at 200 nm, -10.5 % at 160 nm (bulk: -25 %).
k_si_film.source: anchored to M. S. Aubain & P. Bandaru, MRS Proc. 1267, DD12-01 (2010): 260 nm SOI device layer, 90 +/- 10 W/(m K) at room temperature. Cross-checks: Ju & Goodson, APL 74, 3005 (1999) (up to 50 % reduction for films down to 74 nm; fit under-predicts there: 45 vs ~74); Asheghi et al., J. Heat Transfer 120, 30 (1998) (~40 % below bulk at 0.42 um; fit over-predicts: 105 vs ~89)
k_si_film.notes: Corrected by checker 2026-10-09: previous version used d0 = 250 nm (69 W/(m K) at 220 nm), anchored to '32 and 38 W/mK at 50 and 80 nm' attributed to the Aubain & Bandaru MRS paper, which reports only 260 nm, 90 +/- 10 W/(m K). Heavy doping 1e19-1e20: ~80 % of undoped (Electronics Cooling 1998 estimate, assumed). Asheghi et al., J. Appl. Phys. 91, 5079 (2002) covers 1e17-3e19 doped films.

k_sio2.model: k = k300*(T/300)^alpha; kind factor: thermal/fused 1.0, pecvd/beol 0.9
k_sio2.uncertainty_note: +/-10 %; PECVD ~10 % below thermal oxide for films > 100 nm; apparent 0.83-1.23 for 50-500 nm PECVD
k_sio2.source: Palankovski 2000; Corning 7980 data sheet; S.-M. Lee & D. G. Cahill, J. Appl. Phys. 81, 2590 (1997); arXiv:1905.08570

k_low_k.quantity: thermal conductivity of low-k SiOC:H inter-layer dielectric
k_low_k.source: 2014 microfin/IR thermometry study of SiOC:H and SiC:H films (abstract via search)

k_metals.quantity: thermal conductivity of BEOL metals and heater films
k_metals.model: nominal = midpoint of the stated range (Cu BEOL via Wiedemann-Franz with rho 2-2.5 uOhm cm); temperature-independent over 273-400 K (assumed)
k_metals.source: handbook bulk values (assumed); W phonon fraction 62 % (arXiv:2505.07613)

thermal_boundary_resistance.uncertainty_note: Si/SiO2 printed; metal/dielectric ~10x larger (printed ratio, 2008 study), value inferred
thermal_boundary_resistance.source: Lee & Cahill 1997 (equivalent to ~20 nm SiO2); 2008 Cr/PECVD SiO2 study (abstract)
thermal_boundary_resistance.notes: Si/SiO2 is ~1.4 % of a 2 um BOX: negligible. Metal/oxide ~0.25 um oxide equivalent: not negligible for a metal heater <=1 um from the ring.

cp_si.uncertainty_note: within 0.5 % (298 K) and 1.2 % (400 K) of NIST-JANAF (20.000 and 22.142 J/mol K)

density.source: Si standard value; Corning 7980 data sheet (2.201 g/cm3); film ranges assumed
density.notes: SiO2 uses 2200 kg/m^3 (thermal-oxide low end, as in the 02 tables); Corning 7980 prints 2201.

rho_c.model: Si, SiO2: density x Palankovski c_p(T); metals and low-k: constant (assumed)
rho_c.uncertainty_note: Si +/-1.5 %, SiO2 +/-5 %, metals assumed. low-k rho*c is NOT in 02: assumed 1.3 MJ/(m^3 K) from a density of 1.2-1.8 g/cm^3 and an SiO2-like c_p of 0.75-1.0 J/(g K); no source.

plasma_nsm2011.quantity: free-carrier dispersion and absorption, Nedeljkovic-Soref-Mashanovich 2011 (default model)
plasma_nsm2011.model: dalpha = a*dNe^b + c*dNh^d ; dn = -(p*dNe^q + r*dNh^s) (dN in cm^-3)
plasma_nsm2011.valid_range_note: ~1e17-1e20 cm^-3, 300 K; band 1.3 um row used at 1.26-1.36 um (default 'at 1.31 um', 07 P1-7). Tidy3D interpolates the coefficients between the 1.3 and 1.55 rows instead.
plasma_nsm2011.source: M. Nedeljkovic, R. Soref, G. Z. Mashanovich, IEEE Photonics J. 3, 1171 (2011); transcribed from flexcompute/tidy3d default_nedeljkovic_soref_mashanovich_coeffs (primary PDF not opened)

plasma_soref1987.quantity: free-carrier dispersion and absorption, Soref-Bennett 1987 at 1.3 um (switch alternative)
plasma_soref1987.source: R. A. Soref, B. R. Bennett, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 23, 123 (1987)

plasma_temperature.quantity: temperature dependence of the per-carrier plasma dispersion and absorption
plasma_temperature.unit: 1/K (fractional change per K, relative to 300 K)
plasma_temperature.uncertainty_note: no 1.3 um measurement found; nominal = midpoint of the assumed range
plasma_temperature.source: trend from D. M. Riffe, JOSA B 19, 1092 (2002) (effective mass rises with T); magnitudes assumed

plasma_small_signal.quantity: small-signal free-carrier coefficients at 1.3 um (derivatives of NSM 2011; SB 1987 linear)
plasma_small_signal.model: small-signal derivatives of NSM 2011; SB 1987 linear

tpa_beta.quantity: two-photon absorption coefficient of Si at ~1310 nm (for the P2-1 bound tests)
tpa_beta.valid_range_note: ~1.3 um, 300 K; rises with T (1.55 um: 0.76 at 300 K vs 0.42 at 5.5 K, Sinclair 2019); >300 K not measured (assume +0.1 to +0.3 %/K)
tpa_beta.uncertainty_note: 0.5-2.0 cm/GW: factor-3 disagreement between z-scan groups, not resolved
tpa_beta.source: Q. Lin et al., APL 91, 021111 (2007); A. D. Bristow et al., APL 90, 191104 (2007); M. Dinu et al., APL 82, 2954 (2003); G. F. Sinclair et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 11, 044084 (2019)

kerr_n2.quantity: Kerr nonlinear index of Si at ~1310 nm (for the P2-1 bound tests)

free_carrier_lifetime.model: SRH (Borghi: tau_n 35 ns, tau_p 22.5 ns, trap E_i+0.10 eV, 1e15 p-type)
free_carrier_lifetime.uncertainty_note: geometry and surface dependent; reverse-bias value assumed (Turner-Foster 2010 not opened)
free_carrier_lifetime.source: M. Borghi et al., Opt. Express 29, 4363 (2021); D. Dimitropoulos et al., APL 86, 071115 (2005); A. C. Turner-Foster et al., Opt. Express 18, 3582 (2010)
free_carrier_lifetime.notes: Borghi 2021 tau_th = 270 +/- 10 ns is a one-pole lumped fit made with sigma_FCD raised 2-3x, not a measured thermal pole (02 log #20).

doped_si_mobility.quantity: carrier mobility in doped Si (Arora 1982 vs T; Masetti 1983 at 300 K)
doped_si_mobility.model: Arora: mu = mu_min*Tn^a + mu0*T^b/(1 + (N/(Nref*Tn^c))^(alpha0*Tn^d)); Masetti: mu = mu_min1*exp(-Pc/N) + (mu_max - mu_min2)/(1 + (N/Cr)^alpha) - mu1/(1 + (Cs/N)^beta)
doped_si_mobility.valid_range_note: reference table at 23 C; Arora 250-500 K, 1e13-1e20 (weak above 1e19). Unresolved implementation differences: Arora electron Nref 1.26e17 (COMSOL) vs 1.25e17 (nextnano); hole T exponent -2.23 (used) vs -2.33 (one course page).
doped_si_mobility.uncertainty_note: table values printed; models +/-10 % (Arora -13 % at 1e20 n)
doped_si_mobility.source: resistivity-dopant table for c-Si at 23 C (via search); G. Masetti et al., IEEE TED 30, 764 (1983); N. D. Arora et al., IEEE TED 29, 292 (1982) (coefficients via nextnano/DESSIS and COMSOL docs)

doped_si_resistivity.quantity: resistivity of doped single-crystal Si (full ionization, rho = 1/(q N mu))
doped_si_resistivity.model: rho = 1/(q N mu); mu from Masetti (300 K) or Arora (250-500 K), full ionization
doped_si_resistivity.uncertainty_note: table values printed; models +/-10 % (Arora -13 % at 1e20 n)
doped_si_resistivity.source: resistivity-dopant table for c-Si at 23 C (via search); G. Masetti et al., IEEE TED 30, 764 (1983); N. D. Arora et al., IEEE TED 29, 292 (1982) (coefficients via nextnano/DESSIS and COMSOL docs)

doped_si_tcr.quantity: temperature coefficient of resistance of doped Si (Arora mobility, full ionization)
doped_si_tcr.model: TCR = (1/rho) drho/dT with Arora mobility, full ionization
doped_si_tcr.uncertainty_note: +/-50 % (incomplete ionization at 1e17-1e18 lowers it; Arora weak above 1e19)
doped_si_tcr.source: derived from Arora 1982; textbook fit for the G25 heater is 1e-3 /K (REF.heaterTcrPerK, derived)

heater_tcr_family.quantity: heater temperature coefficient of resistance by heater family (07 P1-11)
heater_tcr_family.model: linear R(T) = R0*(1 + TCR*(T - T0)); nominal and range per family

doped_si.source: Arora 1982 mobility, full ionization, 1e18-1e20 cm^-3, 300-375 K (02 §9)

tin.source: AIP Advances 2022 microheater comparison (487 ppm/K); TaN heater patent (~550 ppm/K)
tin.note: low-stress sputtered TiN is nonlinear and can change sign (Sensors & Actuators A 2008)

w.source: bulk handbook 4.5e-3; thick-film patent 4.6e-3; thin-film sign and size set by deposition (Micromachines 2024); lower end 2e-3 shared with silicides (07 P1-11)

heater_tcr_family.rom_family_map_note: metal_above may be TiN or W; its TCR interval spans 0.49e-3 to 4.6e-3 /K
heater_tcr_family.uncertainty_note: process dependent; low-stress TiN nonlinear, can change sign; W film sign depends on deposition; doped Si +/-50 % (incomplete ionization lowers it at 1e17-1e18)
heater_tcr_family.source: AIP Advances 2022 microheater comparison (TiN 487 ppm/C, Pt 2641, Ti 4146); TaN heater patent (TiN ~550 ppm/C); Sensors & Actuators A 2008 (TiN stress); Micromachines 2024 (W films); thick-film W patent (0.0046 /C); Cu, silicides assumed; Arora 1982 (doped Si)

ge_pd_responsivity.model: R = eta*lam[um]/1.23984; assumed constant vs T at 1310 nm (+/-3 % over 0-105 C, assumed)
ge_pd_responsivity.uncertainty_note: T dependence not measured at 1310 nm in sources found; tc range = +/-3 % over 80 K (assumed)
ge_pd_responsivity.source: physics; Lightmatter OFC 2025 talk via textbook REF ([LM-T]); L. Colace et al., J. Lightwave Technol. (2008) (defective Ge loses responsivity with T)

ge_pd_dark_current.quantity: Ge photodiode dark current versus temperature (Arrhenius)
ge_pd_dark_current.uncertainty_note: Ea +/-0.03 eV for the x1.6/10 C reading; device dependent. [checker: Balbi et al., Physica E 2009 (same group) report x1.6-1.9 per 10 C, i.e. Ea up to ~0.5 eV and up to ~x65 at 105 C vs 25 C]
ge_pd_dark_current.source: L. Colace et al. (2008): x1.6 per 10 C; S. J. Koester et al. (2006): x10 at 85 C vs RT (abstracts); GOI p-i-n study (abstract); I_d0 range from 07 D20 (GF prints < 30 nA)
corrections: 02 log #23 / 07 D20: stress Ea 0.5 eV (Balbi 2009, x1.9 per 10 C) kept as an alternative

si_bandgap.source: C. D. Thurmond, J. Electrochem. Soc. 122, 1133 (1975) (as reproduced in device texts)

si_intrinsic_density.source: K. Misiakos, D. Tsamakis, J. Appl. Phys. 74, 3293 (1993); alt. R. Couderc et al., J. Appl. Phys. 115, 093705 (2014): ni = 1.541e15*T^1.712*exp(-Eg0/(2kT)) (Eg0 model not read)

pn_builtin_voltage.quantity: built-in voltage of an abrupt Si PN junction
pn_builtin_voltage.model: Vbi = (kT/q) ln(NA ND / ni(T)^2), step junction, full ionization, no BGN
pn_builtin_voltage.uncertainty_note: band-gap narrowing at ~1e18 lowers Vbi by a few tens of mV (assumed)
